newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mixed, following soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mixed, following soybeans.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended mixed on Friday, in line with soybeans, with nearbys up on a late short-covering rally ahead of the weekend, traders said.
Trade sources pointed to conflicting weather forecasts and said market participants were uncomfortable holding positions through the weekend.

Several private forecasters predicted rainfall of 0.50 to 1.00 inch with high coverage but some local meteorologists said rainfall amounts would be lower with coverage around 30 percent, traders said. Dryness has been of increasing concern in some patches of central Illinois and eastern Iowa.
Soymeal ended $3.40 per ton higher to $0.70 lower with August up $1.80 at $245.60. Soyoil closed 0.06 cent per lb higher to 0.22 cent lower with August up 0.04 at 21.93.
The U.S. Agriculture Department's supply and demand data was viewed as bullish for soyoil and neutral to bearish for soymeal but traders said the influence was short-lived.

USDA put 1997-98 (Sept/Aug) ending soyoil stocks at 1.975 million pounds, down from last month's outlook for two million pounds. The move surprised some who had expected that an increase in soybean output and crush would lead to larger stockpiles.
USDA increased its soyoil production estimate to 16,390 million lbs from 16,220 million last month.
Soyoil exports were forecast to rise by 150 million lbs to 2,050 million.

Meanwhile, soymeal ending supplies were put at 250,000 short tons, up from 200,000 in last month's table. USDA increased soymeal production by 350,000 tons but raised export by only 200,000 tons, traders noted.

On the day, Cargill Inc bought 400 lots August soymeal and 100 lots each September, October and January. ADM bought 200 August and Merrill Lynch bought 200 December and 100 each August, January, March and May. Smith Barney sold 400 August and 100 each September and December.
In soyoil, Cargill Inc bought 300 August and 200 December but sold 200 December and 100 each August and September. Produce Grain sold 600 December and 200 each July and August.
Cargill Inc also bought 500 December 22.00-cent puts, traders said.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 23,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 23,653 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 26,000 lots, against Thursday's 23,899.
